interest: This document provides a concise record of Japanese commercial and economic initiatives in South America during the mid-1930s, specifically highlighting Japanese interest in industrial and hydroelectric investment in Bolivia. It illustrates the State Department's close monitoring of Japanese economic penetration into Latin America during the interwar era. It also demonstrates State Department records-management practices, specifically how cross-reference sheets linked economic matters concerning Japanese capital across decimal classification files.
overview: This file consists of a single State Department document file note (cross-reference sheet) classified under decimal file 894.503124 (Japanese capital investment in Bolivia), directing researchers to Despatch No. 126 dated January 25, 1936, from U.S. Minister Robert G. Caldwell in Bolivia (filed under 624.9417/3). The note summarizes reports concerning the visit of a Japanese Commercial Mission to La Paz to investigate investment opportunities for Japanese capital, specifically evaluating the potential for harnessing water-power to supply electrical equipment for prospective factory construction in Bolivia.

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet noting a despatch on the visit of a Japanese commercial mission exploring capital investment and water-power utilization in La Paz.
subfiles.summary: This document file note indexes Despatch No. 126 of January 25, 1936, from American Minister Robert G. Caldwell in Bolivia, originally filed under 624.9417/3. It records the visit of a Japanese Commercial Mission to La Paz to evaluate opportunities for Japanese capital investment. In particular, the mission surveyed the feasibility of utilizing water power for electrical equipment in support of potential factory construction.
subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet for Despatch No. 126 from Caldwell regarding Japanese capital investment in La Paz
